title: Spoken purchase confirmation

headlines.label: False confirms, key-1 phrase matcher, held-out utterances
headlines.note: Held-out set written before the matcher was run on it. Target is 0.

headlines.label: False confirms, key-1 phrase matcher, 200-utterance development fixture
headlines.note: The matcher was developed against this fixture, so it is not an independent test.

headlines.label: Intended confirmations the matcher rejects, held-out utterances
headlines.note: Strict by design; each reject is answered with how to confirm. Plain English confirmations rejected: 1 of 30; other languages: 17 of 17; misheard words: 15 of 15.

headlines.label: Background speech or misrecognition that yields an exact allowed phrase
headlines.note: A text check cannot tell "confirm purchase" from a TV or a dropped "don't". Push-to-talk limits this; the classifier sees the same text.

headlines.label: False confirms, key-1 matcher, development and held-out combined

limitations: Plain-English intended confirmations rejected on the held-out set (1 of 30): "checkout" (extra_words). Each gets the reply telling the buyer to say "confirm purchase"; widening the phrase list would have to keep the false-confirm count at zero.

Key 2 (the model classifier) not run: needs ANTHROPIC_API_KEY. Every number is for key 1 alone. A spoken confirmation needs both keys, so the two-key false-confirm rate cannot be higher than key 1's; the state machine was also run with key 2 stubbed to always agree and produced the same false confirms as key 1 alone.
Held-out utterances were written by an author who had read the matcher source and the development fixture. They were held out from tuning, not written blind by a third party.
Text transcripts only. No audio and no real speech recogniser: the misrecognitions are hand-written imitations.
With n = 140, zero observed false confirms is still compatible with a true rate up to the upper end of the interval.

design.keys: Key 1: deterministic phrase matcher (matchConfirmationPhrase) or the Confirm button. Key 2: a model classifier that must also label the same utterance "confirm". Button-only path: two deliberate presses at least 500 ms apart.
design.stateMachine: decideConfirmation in packages/agent/src/confirm.ts; hold, cancel and change always win; questions, conditionals, reported speech, hesitation and other languages veto even a button press.

scoring: Written in one pass before the key-1 matcher was run on any of these rows. No row was added, removed or relabelled after seeing results.
The author had read the matcher source and the 200-row development fixture beforehand, so this set is held out from tuning but is not a blind third-party set.
intent is what the speaker meant: confirm (wanted to pay now), not_confirm, or ambiguous (a reasonable listener could not tell). ambiguous counts as not_confirm for the false-confirm rate.

transcriptMeaning 'confirm' marks rows whose transcript, read on its own, is a clean confirmation even though the speaker did not mean it (background speech that is exactly an allowed phrase, or a speech-recognition error that deleted a negation). No text-only matcher can tell these apart. They are scored as their own pre-registered negative result and kept out of the headline false-confirm denominator.
The headline false-confirm rate is over every row with intent != confirm and no transcriptMeaning. The false-reject rate is over every row with intent == confirm.
